newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures forge ahead, funds lead rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures forge ahead, funds lead rally.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures forged sharply higher in late Wednesday trading powered by speculative and fund buying and options-related short-covering.
Consistent industry price-fixing throughout the day also buoyed sentiment and helped push benchmark July up by nearly four percent intraday.
Traders also noted some arbitrage buying. "London is catching up with New York," said one.
By the close, July gained $53 at $1,753 a tonne after hitting the day's top at $1,766, the highest level since March 12.
The contract filled a chart gap at $1,705-$1,730, previously a key barrier, and this triggered light buy stops.
Today's break on the upside of the band set the stage for further headway towards the early March peak at just above $1,800 .
Option-linked short-covering by locals emerged when the market hit above $1,750. Locals sold around the $1,750 calls and hedged on the futures as the market rallied.
Options volume reached a hefty 2,499 lots, with active trading seen in November $1,500 and $2,000 strikes.
Traders noted little overhead origin selling with Indonesian and Thai hedgers looking for much higher values.
There was no fresh fundamental news.
On the supply side, the advent of the main Indonesian harvest could keep a lid on robusta prices.
The new crop would be smaller than last season's but opinions differed on the size of the crop with some refuting suggestions that it could fall by up to 40 percent.

One European trader who had just returned from a crop survey in Indonesia said some farmers had been holding back sales ahead of the May 29 Indonesian general elections and the approaching Brazilian frost season.
Colombia truck drivers ended a day-old strike in the Caribbean port of Cartegana, partially dispelling fears that the action could pread to the rest of the country.
Elsewhere, Dutch roaster Douwe Egberts said on Wednesday it would raise its retail prices by 20 cents per 250-gm pack in response to the sharp rise in world prices.
Brazil is due to auction 200,000 bags of coffee on Wednesday.
